1→---------------------------------------------------------------------------
     2→--- State management for persistent compositor testing.
     3→--
     4→-- This module provides functions to reset compositor state between tests
     5→-- when running in persistent mode (PERSISTENT=1). This allows running
     6→-- multiple tests without restarting the compositor, dramatically improving
     7→-- test suite performance.
     8→--
     9→-- @author somewm contributors
    10→-- @copyright 2025 somewm contributors
    11→-- @module _state
    12→---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    13→
    14→local awful = require("awful")
    15→local gears = require("gears")
    16→local timer = require("gears.timer")
    17→
    18→local state = {}
    19→
    20→-- Track signal connections for cleanup
    21→local tracked_signals = {}
    22→
    23→-- Track timers for cleanup
    24→local tracked_timers = {}
    25→
    26→---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    27→--- Signal Tracking
    28→-- These functions track signal connections so they can be disconnected
    29→-- between tests, preventing test pollution.
    30→---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    31→
    32→--- Connect a signal and track it for later cleanup.
    33→-- Use this instead of obj.connect_signal() in tests to ensure
    34→-- signals are properly disconnected between tests.
    35→-- @tparam table obj Object to connect signal on (e.g., client, screen)
    36→-- @tparam string signal Signal name
    37→-- @tparam function func Handler function
    38→function state.track_signal(obj, signal, func)
    39→    table.insert(tracked_signals, {
    40→        obj = obj,
    41→        signal = signal,
    42→        func = func,
    43→    })
    44→    obj.connect_signal(signal, func)
    45→end
    46→
    47→--- Connect a global signal (on awesome object) and track it.
    48→-- @tparam string signal Signal name
    49→-- @tparam function func Handler function
    50→function state.track_global_signal(signal, func)
    51→    table.insert(tracked_signals, {
    52→        obj = awesome,
    53→        signal = signal,
    54→        func = func,
    55→        is_global = true,
    56→    })
    57→    awesome.connect_signal(signal, func)
    58→end
    59→
    60→--- Disconnect all tracked signals.
    61→-- Called automatically by state.reset().
    62→function state.disconnect_tracked_signals()
    63→    for _, conn in ipairs(tracked_signals) do
    64→        if conn.is_global then
    65→            awesome.disconnect_signal(conn.signal, conn.func)
    66→        else
    67→            conn.obj.disconnect_signal(conn.signal, conn.func)
    68→        end
    69→    end
    70→    tracked_signals = {}
    71→end
    72→
    73→---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    74→--- Timer Tracking
    75→---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    76→
    77→--- Create a timer and track it for cleanup.
    78→-- @tparam table args Timer arguments (same as gears.timer)
    79→-- @treturn timer The created timer
    80→function state.track_timer(args)
    81→    local t = timer(args)
    82→    table.insert(tracked_timers, t)
    83→    return t
    84→end
    85→
    86→--- Stop and remove all tracked timers.
    87→function state.stop_tracked_timers()
    88→    for _, t in ipairs(tracked_timers) do
    89→        if t.started then
    90→            t:stop()
    91→        end
    92→    end
    93→    tracked_timers = {}
    94→end
    95→
    96→---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    97→--- Client Management
    98→---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    99→
   100→--- Kill all managed clients.
   101→-- @tparam[opt=false] boolean force Use SIGKILL instead of graceful close
   102→function state.kill_all_clients(force)
   103→    for _, c in ipairs(client.get()) do
   104→        if force then
   105→            -- Force kill via pid
   106→            local pid = c.pid
   107→            if pid then
   108→                os.execute("kill -9 " .. pid .. " 2>/dev/null")
   109→            end
   110→        else
   111→            c:kill()
   112→        end
   113→    end
   114→end
   115→
   116→--- Wait for all clients to be gone (blocking, for shell script use).
   117→-- Note: This is a blocking wait, only for use in state.reset() via IPC.
   118→-- @tparam[opt=5] number timeout_secs Maximum seconds to wait
   119→-- @treturn boolean True if all clients gone, false if timeout
   120→function state.wait_for_no_clients(timeout_secs)
   121→    timeout_secs = timeout_secs or 5
   122→    local start = os.time()
   123→
   124→    while os.time() - start < timeout_secs do
   125→        if #client.get() == 0 then
   126→            return true
   127→        end
   128→        -- Small yield to allow events to process
   129→        -- Note: This doesn't actually yield in a useful way, but the
   130→        -- shell script will poll the result
   131→    end
   132→
   133→    return false
   134→end
   135→
   136→---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   137→--- Tag Management
   138→---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   139→
   140→--- Reset tags to default test configuration.
   141→-- Creates a single "test" tag per screen with floating layout.
   142→function state.reset_tags()
   143→    for s in screen do
   144→        -- Delete all tags except the first one
   145→        local tags = s.tags
   146→        for i = #tags, 2, -1 do
   147→            tags[i]:delete()
   148→        end
   149→
   150→        -- Reset first tag
   151→        if tags[1] then
   152→            tags[1].name = "test"
   153→            tags[1].layout = awful.layout.suit.floating
   154→            tags[1]:view_only()
   155→            tags[1].selected = true
   156→        else
   157→            -- No tags? Create one
   158→            awful.tag({ "test" }, s, awful.layout.suit.floating)
   159→        end
   160→    end
   161→end
   162→
   163→---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   164→--- Focus Management
   165→---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   166→
   167→--- Clear focus history.
   168→function state.clear_focus_history()
   169→    local aclient = require("awful.client")
   170→    if aclient.focus and aclient.focus.history then
   171→        -- Clear the history list
   172→        if aclient.focus.history.list then
   173→            for i = #aclient.focus.history.list, 1, -1 do
   174→                aclient.focus.history.list[i] = nil
   175→            end
   176→        end
   177→    end
   178→
   179→    -- Clear current focus
   180→    if client.focus then
   181→        client.focus = nil
   182→    end
   183→end
   184→
   185→---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   186→--- Full State Reset
   187→---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   188→
   189→--- Reset all compositor state for a fresh test.
   190→-- Call this between tests when running in persistent mode.
   191→-- @tparam[opt] table options Reset options
   192→-- @tparam[opt=true] boolean options.kill_clients Kill all clients
   193→-- @tparam[opt=true] boolean options.reset_tags Reset tags to defaults
   194→-- @tparam[opt=true] boolean options.clear_focus Clear focus history
   195→-- @tparam[opt=true] boolean options.disconnect_signals Disconnect tracked signals
   196→-- @tparam[opt=true] boolean options.stop_timers Stop tracked timers
   197→-- @treturn boolean True if reset succeeded
   198→function state.reset(options)
   199→    options = options or {}
   200→
   201→    -- Default all options to true
   202→    local kill_clients = options.kill_clients ~= false
   203→    local reset_tags = options.reset_tags ~= false
   204→    local clear_focus = options.clear_focus ~= false
   205→    local disconnect_signals = options.disconnect_signals ~= false
   206→    local stop_timers = options.stop_timers ~= false
   207→
   208→    io.stderr:write("[STATE] Resetting compositor state...\n")
   209→
   210→    -- 1. Stop tracked timers first (prevents interference)
   211→    if stop_timers then
   212→        state.stop_tracked_timers()
   213→    end
   214→
   215→    -- 2. Disconnect tracked signals (prevents spurious events)
   216→    if disconnect_signals then
   217→        state.disconnect_tracked_signals()
   218→    end
   219→
   220→    -- 3. Kill all clients
   221→    if kill_clients then
   222→        state.kill_all_clients(false)
   223→
   224→        -- Wait briefly for clients to close gracefully
   225→        local client_count = #client.get()
   226→        if client_count > 0 then
   227→            io.stderr:write(string.format("[STATE] Waiting for %d clients to close...\n", client_count))
   228→
   229→            -- Poll for up to 2 seconds
   230→            local waited = 0
   231→            while #client.get() > 0 and waited < 20 do
   232→                -- Can't actually sleep here without blocking, so we just
   233→                -- note the count and let the shell script handle waiting
   234→                waited = waited + 1
   235→            end
   236→
   237→            -- Force kill any remaining
   238→            if #client.get() > 0 then
   239→                io.stderr:write("[STATE] Force-killing remaining clients...\n")
   240→                state.kill_all_clients(true)
   241→            end
   242→        end
   243→    end
   244→
   245→    -- 4. Clear focus history
   246→    if clear_focus then
   247→        state.clear_focus_history()
   248→    end
   249→
   250→    -- 5. Reset tags
   251→    if reset_tags then
   252→        state.reset_tags()
   253→    end
   254→
   255→    io.stderr:write("[STATE] Reset complete.\n")
   256→    return true
   257→end
   258→
   259→--- Get current state summary (for debugging).
   260→-- @treturn table State summary
   261→function state.get_summary()
   262→    return {
   263→        client_count = #client.get(),
   264→        screen_count = screen.count(),
   265→        tracked_signals = #tracked_signals,
   266→        tracked_timers = #tracked_timers,
   267→        focused_class = client.focus and client.focus.class or nil,
   268→    }
   269→end
   270→
   271→--- Print state summary to stderr.
   272→function state.debug()
   273→    local s = state.get_summary()
   274→    io.stderr:write(string.format(
   275→        "[STATE] clients=%d screens=%d signals=%d timers=%d focus=%s\n",
   276→        s.client_count, s.screen_count, s.tracked_signals, s.tracked_timers,
   277→        s.focused_class or "nil"
   278→    ))
   279→end
   280→
   281→return state
   282→
   283→-- vim: filetype=lua:expandtab:shiftwidth=4:tabstop=8:softtabstop=4:textwidth=80
   284→

1→---------------------------------------------------------------------------
     2→-- Example test demonstrating the async test API.
     3→--
     4→-- This test shows how to use the new event-driven async primitives
     5→-- instead of magic polling counts. Compare with older tests that use
     6→-- `runner.run_steps()` with `count < 5` style waits.
     7→--
     8→-- Run with: make test-one TEST=tests/test-async-example.lua
     9→---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    10→
    11→local runner = require("_runner")
    12→local async = require("_async")
    13→local test_client = require("_client")
    14→
    15→-- Use runner.run_async() instead of runner.run_steps()
    16→-- The test function runs as a coroutine and can use async.* functions
    17→runner.run_async(function()
    18→    -- Spawn a test client
    19→    -- test_client() returns immediately - client spawns asynchronously
    20→    test_client("async_test_app")
    21→
    22→    -- Wait for client to appear (event-driven, not polling!)
    23→    -- This yields the coroutine until the "manage" signal fires
    24→    -- with a client matching our class, or timeout after 5 seconds
    25→    local c = async.wait_for_client("async_test_app", 5)
    26→
    27→    -- Assert client appeared
    28→    if not c then
    29→        runner.done("Client did not appear within 5 seconds")
    30→        return
    31→    end
    32→
    33→    io.stderr:write("[TEST] Client appeared: " .. tostring(c.class) .. "\n")
    34→
    35→    -- Verify it has focus (new clients get focus by default)
    36→    local focused = async.wait_for_focus("async_test_app", 2)
    37→    if not focused then
    38→        runner.done("Client did not receive focus")
    39→        return
    40→    end
    41→
    42→    io.stderr:write("[TEST] Client has focus\n")
    43→
    44→    -- Test some client properties
    45→    assert(c.valid, "Client should be valid")
    46→    assert(c.class == "async_test_app", "Class should match")
    47→
    48→    -- Kill the client
    49→    -- Note: Terminal running 'sleep infinity' may take a moment to close
    50→    c:kill()
    51→
    52→    -- Wait for client to be gone (give it more time in headless mode)
    53→    local gone = async.wait_for_no_clients(5)
    54→    if not gone then
    55→        -- Force kill any remaining clients
    56→        io.stderr:write("[TEST] Client slow to close, force killing...\n")
    57→        for _, remaining in ipairs(client.get()) do
    58→            if remaining.pid then
    59→                os.execute("kill -9 " .. remaining.pid .. " 2>/dev/null")
    60→            end
    61→        end
    62→        -- Wait a bit more
    63→        async.sleep(0.5)
    64→        gone = async.wait_for_no_clients(2)
    65→        if not gone then
    66→            runner.done("Client did not close even after force kill")
    67→            return
    68→        end
    69→    end
    70→
    71→    io.stderr:write("[TEST] Client closed successfully\n")
    72→
    73→    -- Test passed!
    74→    runner.done()
    75→end)
    76→
    77→-- vim: filetype=lua:expandtab:shiftwidth=4:tabstop=8:softtabstop=4:textwidth=80
    78→

1→---------------------------------------------------------------------------
     2→--- Integration test for client spawning and manipulation.
     3→--
     4→-- This test demonstrates:
     5→-- - Spawning a test client
     6→-- - Waiting for the client to appear
     7→-- - Verifying client properties
     8→-- - Manipulating client geometry
     9→-- - Setting client state (floating, tags)
    10→-- - Cleanup
    11→--
    12→-- @author somewm contributors
    13→-- @copyright 2025 somewm contributors
    14→---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    15→
    16→local runner = require("_runner")
    17→local test_client = require("_client")
    18→local utils = require("_utils")
    19→local awful = require("awful")
    20→
    21→-- Skip test if no terminal available
    22→if not test_client.is_available() then
    23→    io.stderr:write("SKIP: No terminal available for spawning test clients\n")
    24→    io.stderr:write("Test finished successfully.\n")
    25→    awesome.quit()
    26→    return
    27→end
    28→
    29→local terminal_info = test_client.get_terminal_info()
    30→print("Using terminal: " .. terminal_info.executable)
    31→
    32→-- The test client we'll spawn
    33→local c = nil
    34→local test_class = "somewm_test_client"
    35→
    36→local steps = {
    37→    -- Step 1: Spawn a test client
    38→    function(count)
    39→        if count == 1 then
    40→            print("Step 1: Spawning test client with class: " .. test_class)
    41→            test_client(test_class, "Test Window")
    42→        end
    43→
    44→        -- Wait for client to appear
    45→        c = utils.find_client_by_class(test_class)
    46→        if c then
    47→            print("Step 1: Client found!")
    48→            return true
    49→        end
    50→        -- Keep waiting...
    51→    end,
    52→
    53→    -- Step 2: Verify basic client properties
    54→    function()
    55→        print("Step 2: Verifying client properties")
    56→
    57→        assert(c, "Client should exist")
    58→        assert(c.valid, "Client should be valid")
    59→        assert(c.class == test_class,
    60→            string.format("Client class should be '%s', got '%s'", test_class, c.class))
    61→
    62→        -- Client should have a name (window title)
    63→        assert(c.name, "Client should have a name")
    64→        print("  - class: " .. tostring(c.class))
    65→        print("  - name: " .. tostring(c.name))
    66→
    67→        return true
    68→    end,
    69→
    70→    -- Step 3: Test geometry operations
    71→    function()
    72→        print("Step 3: Testing geometry operations")
    73→
    74→        -- Get initial geometry
    75→        local initial_geo = c:geometry()
    76→        print(string.format("  - Initial: x=%d y=%d w=%d h=%d",
    77→            initial_geo.x, initial_geo.y, initial_geo.width, initial_geo.height))
    78→
    79→        -- Set new geometry
    80→        c:geometry({ x = 100, y = 100, width = 400, height = 300 })
    81→
    82→        return true
    83→    end,
    84→
    85→    -- Step 4: Verify geometry was applied
    86→    function()
    87→        local geo = c:geometry()
    88→        print(string.format("  - After set: x=%d y=%d w=%d h=%d",
    89→            geo.x, geo.y, geo.width, geo.height))
    90→
    91→        -- Allow some tolerance for window decorations/borders
    92→        -- The geometry should be close to what we requested
    93→        assert(geo.x >= 0, "x should be non-negative")
    94→        assert(geo.y >= 0, "y should be non-negative")
    95→        assert(geo.width >= 100, "width should be at least 100")
    96→        assert(geo.height >= 100, "height should be at least 100")
    97→
    98→        return true
    99→    end,
   100→
   101→    -- Step 5: Test floating state
   102→    function()
   103→        print("Step 5: Testing floating state")
   104→
   105→        -- Make client floating
   106→        c.floating = true
   107→        assert(c.floating, "Client should be floating")
   108→        print("  - floating: true")
   109→
   110→        -- Make client tiled
   111→        c.floating = false
   112→        assert(not c.floating, "Client should not be floating")
   113→        print("  - floating: false")
   114→
   115→        return true
   116→    end,
   117→
   118→    -- Step 6: Test tag operations
   119→    function()
   120→        print("Step 6: Testing tag operations")
   121→
   122→        local s = c.screen
   123→        local tags = s.tags
   124→        print("  - Screen has " .. #tags .. " tags")
   125→
   126→        if #tags > 0 then
   127→            local first_tag = tags[1]
   128→            c:move_to_tag(first_tag)
   129→
   130→            local client_tags = c:tags()
   131→            assert(#client_tags >= 1, "Client should be on at least one tag")
   132→            print("  - Client is on " .. #client_tags .. " tag(s)")
   133→        end
   134→
   135→        return true
   136→    end,
   137→
   138→    -- Step 7: Test focus
   139→    function()
   140→        print("Step 7: Testing focus")
   141→
   142→        -- Focus the client
   143→        c:activate({ context = "test", raise = true })
   144→
   145→        -- Give it a moment to process
   146→        return true
   147→    end,
   148→
   149→    -- Step 8: Verify focus
   150→    function()
   151→        -- Check if client is focused (may not work perfectly in headless)
   152→        if client.focus == c then
   153→            print("  - Client is focused")
   154→        else
   155→            print("  - Focus: client.focus = " .. tostring(client.focus))
   156→            print("  - (Focus may not work perfectly in headless mode)")
   157→        end
   158→
   159→        return true
   160→    end,
   161→
   162→    -- Step 9: Clean up - kill the client
   163→    function(count)
   164→        if count == 1 then
   165→            print("Step 9: Cleanup - killing client")
   166→            c:kill()
   167→        end
   168→
   169→        -- Check if client is gone
   170→        local clients = client.get()
   171→        if #clients == 0 then
   172→            print("  - Client cleaned up successfully")
   173→            return true
   174→        end
   175→
   176→        -- After a few attempts, force cleanup and proceed
   177→        if count >= 20 then
   178→            print("  - Client still exists after waiting, forcing cleanup")
   179→            -- Force kill via OS (the terminal process)
   180→            local pids = test_client.get_spawned_pids()
   181→            for _, pid in ipairs(pids) do
   182→                os.execute("kill -9 " .. pid .. " 2>/dev/null")
   183→            end
   184→            return true
   185→        end
   186→        -- Keep waiting...
   187→    end,
   188→}
   189→
   190→-- Run the test steps
   191→-- Disable automatic client cleanup since we handle it ourselves
   192→runner.run_steps(steps, { kill_clients = false })
   193→

1→---------------------------------------------------------------------------
     2→--- Test utility functions for somewm integration tests.
     3→--
     4→-- This module provides common helper functions used across integration tests,
     5→-- such as waiting for clients, finding clients by properties, etc.
     6→--
     7→-- @author somewm contributors
     8→-- @copyright 2025 somewm contributors
     9→-- @module _utils
    10→---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    11→
    12→local awful = require("awful")
    13→local gears = require("gears")
    14→
    15→local utils = {}
    16→
    17→--- Find a client by its class/app_id.
    18→-- @tparam string class The class/app_id to search for
    19→-- @treturn client|nil The matching client or nil if not found
    20→function utils.find_client_by_class(class)
    21→    for _, c in ipairs(client.get()) do
    22→        if c.class == class then
    23→            return c
    24→        end
    25→    end
    26→    return nil
    27→end
    28→
    29→--- Find a client by its title/name.
    30→-- @tparam string title The title to search for (exact match)
    31→-- @treturn client|nil The matching client or nil if not found
    32→function utils.find_client_by_title(title)
    33→    for _, c in ipairs(client.get()) do
    34→        if c.name == title then
    35→            return c
    36→        end
    37→    end
    38→    return nil
    39→end
    40→
    41→--- Find clients matching a predicate function.
    42→-- @tparam function matcher Function that takes a client and returns true/false
    43→-- @treturn table List of matching clients
    44→function utils.find_clients(matcher)
    45→    local results = {}
    46→    for _, c in ipairs(client.get()) do
    47→        if matcher(c) then
    48→            table.insert(results, c)
    49→        end
    50→    end
    51→    return results
    52→end
    53→
    54→--- Create a step function that waits for N clients to exist.
    55→-- This is designed to be used directly in runner.run_steps().
    56→-- @tparam number n Number of clients to wait for
    57→-- @treturn function A step function that returns true when N clients exist
    58→function utils.step_wait_for_clients(n)
    59→    return function()
    60→        return #client.get() >= n
    61→    end
    62→end
    63→
    64→--- Create a step function that waits for a client with specific class.
    65→-- @tparam string class The class/app_id to wait for
    66→-- @treturn function A step function that returns the client when found
    67→function utils.step_wait_for_class(class)
    68→    return function()
    69→        local c = utils.find_client_by_class(class)
    70→        return c ~= nil
    71→    end
    72→end
    73→
    74→--- Create a step function that spawns a client on first call, then waits.
    75→-- This is a common pattern: spawn once, then poll until client appears.
    76→-- @tparam function spawn_fn Function to call on first step call
    77→-- @tparam function wait_fn Function that returns true when ready
    78→-- @treturn function A step function for use in runner.run_steps()
    79→function utils.step_spawn_and_wait(spawn_fn, wait_fn)
    80→    local spawned = false
    81→    return function(count)
    82→        if count == 1 and not spawned then
    83→            spawn_fn()
    84→            spawned = true
    85→        end
    86→        return wait_fn()
    87→    end
    88→end
    89→
    90→--- Assert that a geometry matches expected values.
    91→-- Allows for some tolerance due to borders/decorations.
    92→-- @tparam table actual The actual geometry {x, y, width, height}
    93→-- @tparam table expected The expected geometry {x, y, width, height}
    94→-- @tparam[opt=0] number tolerance Allowed difference for each value
    95→function utils.assert_geometry(actual, expected, tolerance)
    96→    tolerance = tolerance or 0
    97→
    98→    local function check(name, a, e)
    99→        if e ~= nil then
   100→            local diff = math.abs(a - e)
   101→            if diff > tolerance then
   102→                error(string.format(
   103→                    "Geometry mismatch: %s expected %d, got %d (diff %d, tolerance %d)",
   104→                    name, e, a, diff, tolerance
   105→                ))
   106→            end
   107→        end
   108→    end
   109→
   110→    check("x", actual.x, expected.x)
   111→    check("y", actual.y, expected.y)
   112→    check("width", actual.width, expected.width)
   113→    check("height", actual.height, expected.height)
   114→end
   115→
   116→--- Assert that a client has expected properties.
   117→-- @tparam client c The client to check
   118→-- @tparam table props Table of property_name = expected_value
   119→function utils.assert_client_props(c, props)
   120→    for prop, expected in pairs(props) do
   121→        local actual = c[prop]
   122→        if actual ~= expected then
   123→            error(string.format(
   124→                "Client property mismatch: %s expected %s, got %s",
   125→                prop, tostring(expected), tostring(actual)
   126→            ))
   127→        end
   128→    end
   129→end
   130→
   131→--- Kill all clients and wait for them to be gone.
   132→-- Returns a step function for use in runner.run_steps().
   133→-- @treturn function A step function that kills all clients
   134→function utils.step_kill_all_clients()
   135→    local killed = false
   136→    return function()
   137→        if not killed then
   138→            for _, c in ipairs(client.get()) do
   139→                c:kill()
   140→            end
   141→            killed = true
   142→        end
   143→        return #client.get() == 0
   144→    end
   145→end
   146→
   147→--- Get the focused screen's workarea.
   148→-- @treturn table The workarea geometry {x, y, width, height}
   149→function utils.get_workarea()
   150→    local s = awful.screen.focused()
   151→    return s and s.workarea or { x = 0, y = 0, width = 1280, height = 720 }
   152→end
   153→
   154→--- Check if we're running in headless mode.
   155→-- @treturn boolean True if running with headless backend
   156→function utils.is_headless()
   157→    return os.getenv("WLR_BACKENDS") == "headless"
   158→end
   159→
   160→---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   161→--- Debug helpers for focus history, signals, and stacking order
   162→-- @section debug_helpers
   163→---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   164→
   165→--- Debug: Print current focus history state.
   166→-- Prints the focus history list with client classes/names for debugging.
   167→-- @tparam[opt=false] boolean verbose Include additional client details
   168→function utils.debug_focus_history(verbose)
   169→    local aclient = require("awful.client")
   170→    local history = aclient.focus.history.list
   171→    local enabled, count = aclient.focus.history.is_enabled()
   172→
   173→    io.stderr:write(string.format(
   174→        "[DEBUG] Focus History: enabled=%s, disabled_count=%d, entries=%d\n",
   175→        tostring(enabled), count or -1, #history
   176→    ))
   177→
   178→    if #history == 0 then
   179→        io.stderr:write("[DEBUG]   (empty)\n")
   180→    else
   181→        for i, c in ipairs(history) do
   182→            if verbose then
   183→                io.stderr:write(string.format(
   184→                    "[DEBUG]   %d: class=%s name=%s valid=%s focused=%s\n",
   185→                    i, tostring(c.class), tostring(c.name),
   186→                    tostring(c.valid), tostring(c == client.focus)
   187→                ))
   188→            else
   189→                io.stderr:write(string.format(
   190→                    "[DEBUG]   %d: class=%s\n", i, tostring(c.class)
   191→                ))
   192→            end
   193→        end
   194→    end
   195→end
   196→
   197→--- Debug: Print all managed clients.
   198→-- @tparam[opt=false] boolean verbose Include geometry and state details
   199→function utils.debug_clients(verbose)
   200→    local clients = client.get()
   201→    io.stderr:write(string.format("[DEBUG] Managed clients: %d\n", #clients))
   202→
   203→    for i, c in ipairs(clients) do
   204→        if verbose then
   205→            local geo = c:geometry()
   206→            io.stderr:write(string.format(
   207→                "[DEBUG]   %d: class=%s name=%s valid=%s visible=%s minimized=%s geo=%dx%d+%d+%d\n",
   208→                i, tostring(c.class), tostring(c.name),
   209→                tostring(c.valid), tostring(c:isvisible()),
   210→                tostring(c.minimized),
   211→                geo.width, geo.height, geo.x, geo.y
   212→            ))
   213→        else
   214→            io.stderr:write(string.format(
   215→                "[DEBUG]   %d: class=%s focused=%s\n",
   216→                i, tostring(c.class), tostring(c == client.focus)
   217→            ))
   218→        end
   219→    end
   220→end
   221→
   222→--- Debug: Print current focused client.
   223→function utils.debug_focused()
   224→    local c = client.focus
   225→    if c then
   226→        io.stderr:write(string.format(
   227→            "[DEBUG] Focused: class=%s name=%s\n",
   228→            tostring(c.class), tostring(c.name)
   229→        ))
   230→    else
   231→        io.stderr:write("[DEBUG] Focused: nil\n")
   232→    end
   233→end
   234→
   235→--- Signal tracker for debugging signal flow from C to Lua.
   236→-- Creates a tracker object that counts signal emissions.
   237→-- @treturn table Signal tracker with connect/get_count/reset methods
   238→function utils.create_signal_tracker()
   239→    local tracker = {
   240→        counts = {},
   241→        log = {},
   242→    }
   243→
   244→    --- Connect to a signal and track its emissions.
   245→    -- @tparam string signal_name The signal name (e.g., "focus", "property::active")
   246→    -- @tparam[opt] object obj Object to connect on (default: client class)
   247→    function tracker:connect(signal_name, obj)
   248→        self.counts[signal_name] = 0
   249→        local target = obj or client
   250→
   251→        target.connect_signal(signal_name, function(c, ...)
   252→            self.counts[signal_name] = (self.counts[signal_name] or 0) + 1
   253→            table.insert(self.log, {
   254→                time = os.time(),
   255→                signal = signal_name,
   256→                client_class = c and c.class or nil,
   257→                args = {...}
   258→            })
   259→            io.stderr:write(string.format(
   260→                "[SIGNAL] %s fired (count=%d) client=%s\n",
   261→                signal_name, self.counts[signal_name],
   262→                c and c.class or "nil"
   263→            ))
   264→        end)
   265→    end
   266→
   267→    --- Connect to a global signal on awesome object.
   268→    -- @tparam string signal_name The signal name (e.g., "client::focus")
   269→    function tracker:connect_global(signal_name)
   270→        self.counts[signal_name] = 0
   271→
   272→        awesome.connect_signal(signal_name, function(...)
   273→            self.counts[signal_name] = (self.counts[signal_name] or 0) + 1
   274→            table.insert(self.log, {
   275→                time = os.time(),
   276→                signal = signal_name,
   277→                args = {...}
   278→            })
   279→            io.stderr:write(string.format(
   280→                "[SIGNAL] global %s fired (count=%d)\n",
   281→                signal_name, self.counts[signal_name]
   282→            ))
   283→        end)
   284→    end
   285→
   286→    --- Get the count for a specific signal.
   287→    -- @tparam string signal_name The signal to check
   288→    -- @treturn number The emission count
   289→    function tracker:get_count(signal_name)
   290→        return self.counts[signal_name] or 0
   291→    end
   292→
   293→    --- Reset all counts.
   294→    function tracker:reset()
   295→        for k in pairs(self.counts) do
   296→            self.counts[k] = 0
   297→        end
   298→        self.log = {}
   299→    end
   300→
   301→    --- Print summary of all tracked signals.
   302→    function tracker:print_summary()
   303→        io.stderr:write("[SIGNAL SUMMARY]\n")
   304→        for name, count in pairs(self.counts) do
   305→            io.stderr:write(string.format("  %s: %d\n", name, count))
   306→        end
   307→    end
   308→
   309→    return tracker
   310→end
   311→
   312→--- DEPRECATED: Wait for a condition with debug output.
   313→-- WARNING: This function uses a blocking busy-wait loop that freezes the
   314→-- event loop. Use async.wait_for_condition() instead for non-blocking waits.
   315→--
   316→-- @deprecated Use async.wait_for_condition() from _async.lua instead
   317→-- @tparam string description What we're waiting for
   318→-- @tparam function condition Function that returns true when done
   319→-- @tparam[opt=5] number max_seconds Maximum seconds to wait
   320→-- @treturn boolean True if condition met, false if timed out
   321→function utils.wait_for(description, condition, max_seconds)
   322→    io.stderr:write("[DEPRECATED] utils.wait_for() blocks the event loop! Use async.wait_for_condition() instead.\n")
   323→
   324→    max_seconds = max_seconds or 5
   325→    local start = os.time()
   326→
   327→    io.stderr:write(string.format("[WAIT] %s...\n", description))
   328→
   329→    while os.time() - start < max_seconds do
   330→        if condition() then
   331→            io.stderr:write(string.format("[WAIT] %s: OK\n", description))
   332→            return true
   333→        end
   334→        -- WARNING: This busy-wait blocks the compositor event loop!
   335→    end
   336→
   337→    io.stderr:write(string.format("[WAIT] %s: TIMEOUT\n", description))
   338→    return false
   339→end
   340→
   341→--- Create a step that verifies focus history contains expected entries.
   342→-- @tparam table expected_classes List of classes in expected order (most recent first)
   343→-- @treturn function Step function for runner.run_steps()
   344→function utils.step_verify_focus_history(expected_classes)
   345→    return function()
   346→        local aclient = require("awful.client")
   347→        local history = aclient.focus.history.list
   348→
   349→        if #history < #expected_classes then
   350→            return nil -- Not enough entries yet, keep waiting
   351→        end
   352→
   353→        -- Verify order matches
   354→        for i, expected_class in ipairs(expected_classes) do
   355→            local c = history[i]
   356→            if not c or c.class ~= expected_class then
   357→                io.stderr:write(string.format(
   358→                    "[VERIFY] Focus history mismatch at %d: expected=%s got=%s\n",
   359→                    i, expected_class, c and c.class or "nil"
   360→                ))
   361→                return false
   362→            end
   363→        end
   364→
   365→        io.stderr:write("[VERIFY] Focus history matches expected order\n")
   366→        return true
   367→    end
   368→end
   369→
   370→--- Create a step that waits for focus to be on a specific client class.
   371→-- @tparam string class The class/app_id to wait for
   372→-- @treturn function Step function for runner.run_steps()
   373→function utils.step_wait_for_focus(class)
   374→    return function()
   375→        local c = client.focus
   376→        if c and c.class == class then
   377→            return true
   378→        end
   379→        return nil -- Keep waiting
   380→    end
   381→end
   382→
   383→--- Activate a client and verify focus.
   384→-- Helper to properly activate a client using request::activate signal.
   385→-- @tparam client c The client to activate
   386→-- @tparam[opt="test"] string context Activation context
   387→function utils.activate_client(c, context)
   388→    context = context or "test"
   389→    c:emit_signal("request::activate", context, { raise = true })
   390→end
   391→
   392→---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   393→--- TDD assertion helpers
   394→-- @section assertions
   395→---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   396→
   397→--- Assert that focus is on a specific client class (or nil).
   398→-- Throws an error with descriptive message if assertion fails.
   399→-- @tparam string|nil expected_class Expected class name, or nil for no focus
   400→function utils.assert_focus(expected_class)
   401→    local c = client.focus
   402→    if expected_class == nil then
   403→        if c ~= nil then
   404→            error(string.format(
   405→                "Expected no focus, got %s",
   406→                c.class or "unknown"
   407→            ), 2)
   408→        end
   409→    else
   410→        if c == nil then
   411→            error(string.format(
   412→                "Expected focus on '%s', got nil",
   413→                expected_class
   414→            ), 2)
   415→        elseif c.class ~= expected_class then
   416→            error(string.format(
   417→                "Expected focus on '%s', got '%s'",
   418→                expected_class, c.class or "unknown"
   419→            ), 2)
   420→        end
   421→    end
   422→end
   423→
   424→--- Assert that a signal was emitted exactly N times.
   425→-- @tparam table tracker Signal tracker created by create_signal_tracker()
   426→-- @tparam string signal_name The signal to check
   427→-- @tparam number expected Expected emission count
   428→function utils.assert_signal_count(tracker, signal_name, expected)
   429→    local actual = tracker:get_count(signal_name)
   430→    if actual ~= expected then
   431→        error(string.format(
   432→            "Signal '%s': expected %d emissions, got %d",
   433→            signal_name, expected, actual
   434→        ), 2)
   435→    end
   436→end
   437→
   438→--- Assert the current number of managed clients.
   439→-- @tparam number expected Expected client count
   440→function utils.assert_client_count(expected)
   441→    local actual = #client.get()
   442→    if actual ~= expected then
   443→        error(string.format(
   444→            "Expected %d clients, got %d",
   445→            expected, actual
   446→        ), 2)
   447→    end
   448→end
   449→
   450→--- Assert that a condition is true, with custom message.
   451→-- Like Lua's assert but with better error level for test output.
   452→-- @tparam boolean condition The condition to check
   453→-- @tparam string message Error message if condition is false
   454→function utils.assert_true(condition, message)
   455→    if not condition then
   456→        error(message or "Assertion failed", 2)
   457→    end
   458→end
   459→

1→---------------------------------------------------------------------------
     2→--- X11/XWayland test client helper for somewm integration tests.
     3→--
     4→-- This module provides a way to spawn X11 applications for testing XWayland
     5→-- support. It mirrors the _client.lua API but spawns X11 apps via XWayland.
     6→--
     7→-- @author somewm contributors
     8→-- @copyright 2025 somewm contributors
     9→-- @module _x11_client
    10→---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    11→
    12→local awful = require("awful")
    13→local gears = require("gears")
    14→
    15→local module = {}
    16→
    17→-- Track spawned test client PIDs for cleanup
    18→local spawned_pids = {}
    19→
    20→-- Detect which X11 terminal/app is available for spawning test clients
    21→local x11_app_cmd = nil
    22→local x11_detected = false
    23→
    24→local function detect_x11_app()
    25→    if x11_detected then
    26→        return x11_app_cmd ~= nil
    27→    end
    28→    x11_detected = true
    29→
    30→    -- Try X11 terminals/apps in order of preference
    31→    -- Each entry: { executable, class_flag, exec_flag, default_class }
    32→    -- xterm is preferred because it's widely available and has reliable -class
    33→    local apps = {
    34→        -- xterm: -class sets WM_CLASS resource class, -name sets instance
    35→        { "xterm", "-class", "-e", "XTerm" },
    36→        -- xeyes: simple X11 app, good for visual tests (no exec flag)
    37→        { "xeyes", nil, nil, "XEyes" },
    38→        -- xclock: another simple X11 app
    39→        { "xclock", nil, nil, "XClock" },
    40→    }
    41→
    42→    for _, app in ipairs(apps) do
    43→        local exe = app[1]
    44→        local handle = io.popen("which " .. exe .. " 2>/dev/null")
    45→        if handle then
    46→            local result = handle:read("*a")
    47→            handle:close()
    48→            if result and result:match(exe) then
    49→                x11_app_cmd = app
    50→                return true
    51→            end
    52→        end
    53→    end
    54→
    55→    io.stderr:write("WARNING: No X11 application found for XWayland tests\n")
    56→    io.stderr:write("  Tried: xterm, xeyes, xclock\n")
    57→    io.stderr:write("  Install one of these to run XWayland tests\n")
    58→    return false
    59→end
    60→
    61→--- Spawn an X11 test client with the given class.
    62→-- @tparam[opt="xwayland_test"] string class The WM_CLASS for the client
    63→-- @tparam[opt] string title The window title (may not be honored by all apps)
    64→-- @treturn number|nil The PID of the spawned process, or nil on failure
    65→local function spawn_x11_client(_, class, title)
    66→    class = class or "xwayland_test"
    67→
    68→    if not detect_x11_app() then
    69→        io.stderr:write("ERROR: Cannot spawn X11 test client - no X11 app available\n")
    70→        return nil
    71→    end
    72→
    73→    local exe = x11_app_cmd[1]
    74→    local class_flag = x11_app_cmd[2]
    75→    local exec_flag = x11_app_cmd[3]
    76→
    77→    -- Build command based on what app we're using
    78→    local cmd
    79→    if exe == "xterm" then
    80→        -- xterm: -class CLASS -name INSTANCE -T TITLE -e CMD
    81→        cmd = string.format(
    82→            "xterm -class %s -name %s -T '%s' -e 'sleep infinity'",
    83→            class, class:lower(), title or class
    84→        )
    85→    elseif exe == "xeyes" or exe == "xclock" then
    86→        -- These simple apps don't support class override easily,
    87→        -- but we can still spawn them for basic XWayland testing
    88→        cmd = exe
    89→        io.stderr:write(string.format(
    90→            "WARNING: %s doesn't support custom WM_CLASS, using default\n", exe
    91→        ))
    92→    else
    93→        -- Generic fallback
    94→        if class_flag then
    95→            cmd = string.format("%s %s %s", exe, class_flag, class)
    96→        else
    97→            cmd = exe
    98→        end
    99→    end
   100→
   101→    io.stderr:write(string.format("[X11] Spawning: %s\n", cmd))
   102→
   103→    -- Spawn the client
   104→    local pid = awful.spawn(cmd)
   105→
   106→    if pid and type(pid) == "number" and pid > 0 then
   107→        table.insert(spawned_pids, pid)
   108→        return pid
   109→    else
   110→        io.stderr:write("ERROR: Failed to spawn X11 test client: " .. tostring(pid) .. "\n")
   111→        return nil
   112→    end
   113→end
   114→
   115→--- Terminate all spawned X11 test clients.
   116→-- This should be called at the end of tests to clean up.
   117→function module.terminate()
   118→    for _, pid in ipairs(spawned_pids) do
   119→        os.execute("kill " .. pid .. " 2>/dev/null")
   120→    end
   121→    spawned_pids = {}
   122→end
   123→
   124→--- Get the list of spawned PIDs.
   125→-- @treturn table List of PIDs for spawned X11 test clients
   126→function module.get_spawned_pids()
   127→    return gears.table.clone(spawned_pids)
   128→end
   129→
   130→--- Check if an X11 application is available for spawning.
   131→-- @treturn boolean True if an X11 app was detected
   132→function module.is_available()
   133→    return detect_x11_app()
   134→end
   135→
   136→--- Get info about the detected X11 application.
   137→-- @treturn table|nil Table with app info or nil
   138→function module.get_app_info()
   139→    if detect_x11_app() then
   140→        return {
   141→            executable = x11_app_cmd[1],
   142→            class_flag = x11_app_cmd[2],
   143→            exec_flag = x11_app_cmd[3],
   144→            default_class = x11_app_cmd[4],
   145→        }
   146→    end
   147→    return nil
   148→end
   149→
   150→--- Get the default WM_CLASS for spawned X11 clients.
   151→-- This is useful when the app doesn't support custom class names.
   152→-- @treturn string|nil The default class name
   153→function module.get_default_class()
   154→    if detect_x11_app() then
   155→        -- For xterm with custom class, return what we'll set
   156→        if x11_app_cmd[1] == "xterm" then
   157→            return nil -- We set custom class
   158→        end
   159→        return x11_app_cmd[4]
   160→    end
   161→    return nil
   162→end
   163→
   164→--- Check if a client is an XWayland client.
   165→-- @tparam client c The client to check
   166→-- @treturn boolean True if client is XWayland
   167→function module.is_xwayland(c)
   168→    -- XWayland clients have a window ID (X11 window)
   169→    -- Native Wayland clients don't
   170→    return c and c.window and c.window > 0
   171→end
   172→
   173→--- Find X11 clients by class.
   174→-- @tparam string class The WM_CLASS to search for
   175→-- @treturn table List of matching X11 clients
   176→function module.find_by_class(class)
   177→    local results = {}
   178→    for _, c in ipairs(client.get()) do
   179→        if c.class == class and module.is_xwayland(c) then
   180→            table.insert(results, c)
   181→        end
   182→    end
   183→    return results
   184→end
   185→
   186→-- Make the module callable for spawning clients
   187→-- Usage: x11_client("MyXApp", "Window Title")
   188→return setmetatable(module, { __call = spawn_x11_client })
   189→
   190→-- vim: filetype=lua:expandtab:shiftwidth=4:tabstop=8:softtabstop=4:textwidth=80
   191→

1→---------------------------------------------------------------------------
     2→--- Test: XWayland keyboard focus
     3→--
     4→-- Verifies that XWayland (X11) clients properly receive keyboard focus
     5→-- when they are spawned/activated, without requiring mouse hover.
     6→--
     7→-- This test validates the fix for the XWayland focus bug where X11 apps
     8→-- wouldn't receive keyboard input until the user hovered over them.
     9→--
    10→-- NOTE: This test requires visual mode (HEADLESS=0) because XWayland
    11→-- needs a display.
    12→---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    13→
    14→local runner = require("_runner")
    15→local test_client = require("_client")
    16→local x11_client = require("_x11_client")
    17→local utils = require("_utils")
    18→
    19→-- Check if we're in headless mode (XWayland won't work properly)
    20→local function is_headless()
    21→    local backend = os.getenv("WLR_BACKENDS")
    22→    return backend == "headless"
    23→end
    24→
    25→-- Skip test if requirements not met
    26→if is_headless() then
    27→    io.stderr:write("SKIP: XWayland tests require visual mode (HEADLESS=0)\n")
    28→    io.stderr:write("Test finished successfully.\n")
    29→    awesome.quit()
    30→    return
    31→end
    32→
    33→if not x11_client.is_available() then
    34→    io.stderr:write("SKIP: no X11 application available (install xterm)\n")
    35→    io.stderr:write("Test finished successfully.\n")
    36→    awesome.quit()
    37→    return
    38→end
    39→
    40→local my_x11_client
    41→
    42→local steps = {
    43→    -- Step 1: Spawn an X11 client
    44→    function(count)
    45→        if count == 1 then
    46→            io.stderr:write("[TEST] Spawning X11 client...\n")
    47→            x11_client("xwayland_focus_test")
    48→        end
    49→
    50→        -- Look for the X11 client
    51→        -- Note: xterm sets WM_CLASS to what we specify
    52→        for _, c in ipairs(client.get()) do
    53→            if c.class == "xwayland_focus_test" or
    54→               (c.class == "XTerm" and x11_client.is_xwayland(c)) then
    55→                my_x11_client = c
    56→                io.stderr:write(string.format(
    57→                    "[TEST] X11 client spawned: class=%s, window=%s, is_x11=%s\n",
    58→                    c.class, tostring(c.window), tostring(x11_client.is_xwayland(c))
    59→                ))
    60→                return true
    61→            end
    62→        end
    63→
    64→        -- Timeout after ~5 seconds
    65→        if count > 50 then
    66→            io.stderr:write("[TEST] ERROR: X11 client did not appear\n")
    67→            error("X11 client did not spawn within timeout")
    68→        end
    69→
    70→        return nil
    71→    end,
    72→
    73→    -- Step 2: Verify the X11 client is an XWayland client
    74→    function()
    75→        assert(x11_client.is_xwayland(my_x11_client),
    76→            "Expected client to be XWayland (have X11 window ID)")
    77→        io.stderr:write(string.format(
    78→            "[TEST] Confirmed XWayland client: window=%d\n",
    79→            my_x11_client.window or 0
    80→        ))
    81→        return true
    82→    end,
    83→
    84→    -- Step 3: Wait a moment for focus to settle, then verify X11 client has REAL keyboard focus
    85→    function(count)
    86→        -- Give focus a moment to be set (this is the bug we're testing!)
    87→        if count < 5 then
    88→            return nil
    89→        end
    90→
    91→        -- Check ACTUAL keyboard focus, not just client.focus (Lua bookkeeping)
    92→        -- has_keyboard_focus() checks wlroots seat->keyboard_state.focused_surface
    93→        local has_real_focus = my_x11_client:has_keyboard_focus()
    94→
    95→        io.stderr:write(string.format(
    96→            "[TEST] Checking focus (attempt %d): client.focus=%s, has_keyboard_focus=%s\n",
    97→            count,
    98→            client.focus and client.focus.class or "nil",
    99→            tostring(has_real_focus)
   100→        ))
   101→
   102→        -- THE KEY ASSERTION: X11 client should have REAL keyboard focus immediately
   103→        -- without requiring mouse hover. This is the actual wlroots seat focus,
   104→        -- not just Lua bookkeeping.
   105→        if has_real_focus then
   106→            io.stderr:write("[TEST] PASS: X11 client has REAL keyboard focus\n")
   107→            return true
   108→        end
   109→
   110→        -- Timeout - this is the failure case that indicates the bug
   111→        if count > 20 then
   112→            error(string.format(
   113→                "FAIL: X11 client does not have REAL keyboard focus. " ..
   114→                "client.focus=%s but has_keyboard_focus()=%s. " ..
   115→                "This indicates the XWayland focus bug is present.",
   116→                client.focus and client.focus.class or "nil",
   117→                tostring(has_real_focus)
   118→            ))
   119→        end
   120→
   121→        return nil
   122→    end,
   123→
   124→    -- Step 4: Cleanup
   125→    function(count)
   126→        if count == 1 then
   127→            io.stderr:write("[TEST] Cleanup: killing X11 client\n")
   128→            if my_x11_client and my_x11_client.valid then
   129→                my_x11_client:kill()
   130→            end
   131→            -- Also kill via pkill as backup
   132→            os.execute("pkill -9 xterm 2>/dev/null")
   133→        end
   134→
   135→        if #client.get() == 0 then
   136→            io.stderr:write("[TEST] Cleanup: done\n")
   137→            return true
   138→        end
   139→
   140→        if count >= 10 then
   141→            io.stderr:write("[TEST] Cleanup: force killing\n")
   142→            local pids = x11_client.get_spawned_pids()
   143→            for _, pid in ipairs(pids) do
   144→                os.execute("kill -9 " .. pid .. " 2>/dev/null")
   145→            end
   146→            return true
   147→        end
   148→    end,
   149→}
   150→
   151→runner.run_steps(steps, { kill_clients = false })
   152→
   153→-- vim: filetype=lua:expandtab:shiftwidth=4:tabstop=8:softtabstop=4:textwidth=80
   154→

  - `runner.run_async(test_fn, options)` - Coroutine-based async tests
  - `runner.done(message)` - Signal test completion
  - Each step returns: `true` (pass/continue), `false` (fail), `nil` (retry in 100ms)
  - Auto-kills clients at end via `runner.step_kill_clients`
  - Persistent mode support (don't quit compositor between tests)

  - `async.wait_for_signal(obj, signal_name, timeout_secs, filter)` - Signal-based waiting
  - `async.wait_for_condition(condition, timeout_secs, poll_interval)` - Condition polling
  - `async.wait_for_client(class, timeout_secs)` - Wait for client to appear
  - `async.wait_for_focus(class, timeout_secs)` - Wait for focus change
  - `async.wait_for_client_count(count, timeout_secs)`
  - `async.wait_for_no_clients(timeout_secs)`
  - `async.sleep(secs)` - Non-blocking sleep
  - Uses coroutines for clean, semantic test code

- **`/home/box/git/github/somewm/tests/_client.lua`** (143 lines)
  - Spawns Wayland test clients (kitty, foot, alacritty, ghostty)

  - `test_client(class, title)` - Callable module to spawn clients

  - `test_client.get_spawned_pids()` - Get spawned process IDs
  - Uses `sleep infinity` with `--class` flag for control

  - `x11_client.is_xwayland(c)` - Check if client is X11 (has window ID > 0)
  - `x11_client.find_by_class(class)` - Find X11 clients
  - X11-specific: checks `c.window` property (X11 window ID)

  - `state.reset(options)` - Full state reset between tests
  - `state.kill_all_clients(force)` - Kill all clients

  - `state.track_timer(args)` - Track timers for cleanup
  - `state.get_summary()` - Debug state snapshot

  - Error redirect to stderr for visibility

### 3. Integration Test Execution Modes

**From Makefile targets:**

```makefile
make test                    # All tests (fast, no ASAN)
make test-unit              # Unit tests only (busted)
make test-integration       # Integration tests (visual mode)
make test-asan              # Integration tests with ASAN (catches memory bugs)
make test-ci                # Headless for CI (HEADLESS=1)
make test-fast              # Persistent mode (10x faster, PERSISTENT=1)
make test-one TEST=tests/test-focus.lua  # Single test with verbose
make test-visual            # Visual mode (HEADLESS=0, watch tests)
make test-one-visual        # Single test visual debug
```

**Environment variables control behavior:**

- `HEADLESS=1` - headless backend (reliable for CI)
- `HEADLESS=0` - Wayland backend (visual debugging, needs parent Wayland)
- `PERSISTENT=1` - Keep compositor running between tests (reset state, 10x faster)
- `PERSISTENT=0` - Fresh compositor per test (slower, more isolated)
- `VERBOSE=1` - Show test names and output
- `TEST_TIMEOUT=30` - Per-test timeout in seconds
- `TEST_RC_LUA` - Custom rc.lua for tests

**Runner script** `/home/box/git/github/somewm/tests/run-integration.sh`:

1. Creates isolated temp directory and config
2. Sets up `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR` or unique socket for test compositor
3. Starts somewm with test config (90-second startup timeout)
4. Waits for IPC socket to appear
5. Tests run via: `somewm-client eval "dofile('tests/test-foo.lua')"`
6. Monitors log for "Test finished successfully." marker
7. Kills compositor and cleans up

**Test lifecycle:**

1. Test file loaded and executed in compositor's Lua context
2. Calls `runner.run_steps(steps)` or `runner.run_async(fn)` 
3. Steps execute with 2-second timeout per step (retries every 100ms)

**Step-based (traditional polling):**

local steps = {
    function(count)  -- count = number of times step called

**Environment variables control behavior:**

### 4. How Integration Tests Work

**Runner script** `/home/box/git/github/somewm/tests/run-integration.sh`:

1. Creates isolated temp directory and config
2. Sets up `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR` or unique socket for test compositor
3. Starts somewm with test config (90-second startup timeout)
4. Waits for IPC socket to appear
5. Tests run via: `somewm-client eval "dofile('tests/test-foo.lua')"`
6. Monitors log for "Test finished successfully." marker
7. Kills compositor and cleans up

**Test lifecycle:**

1. Test file loaded and executed in compositor's Lua context
2. Calls `runner.run_steps(steps)` or `runner.run_async(fn)` 
3. Steps execute with 2-second timeout per step (retries every 100ms)
4. On success: "Test finished successfully." written to stderr
5. Compositor can optionally run in persistent mode (faster)

**Step-based (traditional polling):**
```lua
local steps = {
    function(count)  -- count = number of times step called
        if count == 1 then
            test_client("myapp")  -- Called once on first try
        end
        local c = utils.find_client_by_class("myapp")
        return c ~= nil  -- true=pass, nil=retry, false=fail
    end,
}
runner.run_steps(steps)
```

**Async (event-driven, recommended):**
```lua
runner.run_async(function()
    test_client("myapp")
    local c = async.wait_for_client("myapp", 5)  -- Yields until signal fires
    assert(c, "Client should appear")
    runner.done()  -- Signal success (replaces return)
end)
```

---------------------------------------------------------------------------
--- Test: XWayland configure/geometry handling
--
-- Verifies that XWayland (X11) clients properly receive geometry updates
-- and that programmatic geometry changes work correctly.
--
-- This tests that:
-- 1. X11 clients can have their geometry changed programmatically
-- 2. X11 clients respect geometry constraints
-- 3. X11 clients are properly positioned on screen
--
-- NOTE: This test requires visual mode (HEADLESS=0) because XWayland
-- needs a display.
---------------------------------------------------------------------------

local runner = require("_runner")
local test_client = require("_client")
local x11_client = require("_x11_client")
local utils = require("_utils")

-- Check if we're in headless mode
local function is_headless()
    local backend = os.getenv("WLR_BACKENDS")
    return backend == "headless"
end

-- Skip test if requirements not met
if is_headless() then
    io.stderr:write("SKIP: XWayland tests require visual mode (HEADLESS=0)\n")
    io.stderr:write("Test finished successfully.\n")
    awesome.quit()
    return
end

if not x11_client.is_available() then
    io.stderr:write("SKIP: no X11 application available (install xterm)\n")
    io.stderr:write("Test finished successfully.\n")
    awesome.quit()
    return
end

local my_x11_client

local steps = {
    -- Step 1: Spawn an X11 client
    function(count)
        if count == 1 then
            io.stderr:write("[TEST] Spawning X11 client...\n")
            x11_client("xw_configure_test")
        end

        for _, c in ipairs(client.get()) do
            if c.class == "xw_configure_test" or
               (c.class == "XTerm" and x11_client.is_xwayland(c)) then
                my_x11_client = c
                io.stderr:write(string.format(
                    "[TEST] X11 client spawned: class=%s, geom=%dx%d+%d+%d\n",
                    c.class, c.width, c.height, c.x, c.y
                ))
                return true
            end
        end

        if count > 50 then
            error("X11 client did not spawn within timeout")
        end

        return nil
    end,

    -- Step 2: Wait for client to settle
    function(count)
        if count < 5 then
            return nil
        end

        -- Verify client has valid geometry
        assert(my_x11_client.width > 0, "Client width should be > 0")
        assert(my_x11_client.height > 0, "Client height should be > 0")

        io.stderr:write(string.format(
            "[TEST] Initial geometry: %dx%d+%d+%d\n",
            my_x11_client.width, my_x11_client.height,
            my_x11_client.x, my_x11_client.y
        ))
        return true
    end,

    -- Step 3: Change geometry programmatically
    function(count)
        if count == 1 then
            io.stderr:write("[TEST] Setting geometry to 400x300+100+100...\n")
            my_x11_client:geometry({ x = 100, y = 100, width = 400, height = 300 })
        end

        if count < 5 then
            return nil
        end

        local geom = my_x11_client:geometry()
        io.stderr:write(string.format(
            "[TEST] After geometry set: %dx%d+%d+%d\n",
            geom.width, geom.height, geom.x, geom.y
        ))

        -- Allow some tolerance for window decorations/borders
        local width_ok = math.abs(geom.width - 400) <= 10
        local height_ok = math.abs(geom.height - 300) <= 10

        if width_ok and height_ok then
            io.stderr:write("[TEST] PASS: Geometry change applied\n")
            return true
        end

        if count > 20 then
            error(string.format(
                "FAIL: Geometry not applied. Expected ~400x300, got %dx%d",
                geom.width, geom.height
            ))
        end

        return nil
    end,

    -- Step 4: Test moving the window
    function(count)
        if count == 1 then
            io.stderr:write("[TEST] Moving window to 200,200...\n")
            my_x11_client.x = 200
            my_x11_client.y = 200
        end

        if count < 5 then
            return nil
        end

        local x_ok = math.abs(my_x11_client.x - 200) <= 10
        local y_ok = math.abs(my_x11_client.y - 200) <= 10

        if x_ok and y_ok then
            io.stderr:write(string.format(
                "[TEST] PASS: Window moved to %d,%d\n",
                my_x11_client.x, my_x11_client.y
            ))
            return true
        end

        if count > 20 then
            error(string.format(
                "FAIL: Window not moved. Expected ~200,200, got %d,%d",
                my_x11_client.x, my_x11_client.y
            ))
        end

        return nil
    end,

    -- Step 5: Cleanup
    function(count)
        if count == 1 then
            io.stderr:write("[TEST] Cleanup: killing X11 client\n")
            if my_x11_client and my_x11_client.valid then
                my_x11_client:kill()
            end
            os.execute("pkill -9 xterm 2>/dev/null")
        end

        if #client.get() == 0 then
            io.stderr:write("[TEST] Cleanup: done\n")
            return true
        end

        if count >= 10 then
            io.stderr:write("[TEST] Cleanup: force killing\n")
            local pids = x11_client.get_spawned_pids()
            for _, pid in ipairs(pids) do
                os.execute("kill -9 " .. pid .. " 2>/dev/null")
            end
            return true
        end
    end,
}

runner.run_steps(steps, { kill_clients = false })

---------------------------------------------------------------------------
--- X11/XWayland test client helper for somewm integration tests.
--
-- This module provides a way to spawn X11 applications for testing XWayland
-- support. It mirrors the _client.lua API but spawns X11 apps via XWayland.
--
-- @author somewm contributors
-- @copyright 2025 somewm contributors
-- @module _x11_client
---------------------------------------------------------------------------

local awful = require("awful")
local gears = require("gears")

local module = {}

-- Track spawned test client PIDs for cleanup
local spawned_pids = {}

-- Detect which X11 terminal/app is available for spawning test clients
local x11_app_cmd = nil
local x11_detected = false

local function detect_x11_app()
    if x11_detected then
        return x11_app_cmd ~= nil
    end
    x11_detected = true

    -- Try X11 terminals/apps in order of preference
    -- Each entry: { executable, class_flag, exec_flag, default_class }
    -- xterm is preferred because it's widely available and has reliable -class
    local apps = {
        -- xterm: -class sets WM_CLASS resource class, -name sets instance
        { "xterm", "-class", "-e", "XTerm" },
        -- xeyes: simple X11 app, good for visual tests (no exec flag)
        { "xeyes", nil, nil, "XEyes" },
        -- xclock: another simple X11 app
        { "xclock", nil, nil, "XClock" },
    }

    for _, app in ipairs(apps) do
        local exe = app[1]
        local handle = io.popen("which " .. exe .. " 2>/dev/null")
        if handle then
            local result = handle:read("*a")
            handle:close()
            if result and result:match(exe) then
                x11_app_cmd = app
                return true
            end
        end
    end

    io.stderr:write("WARNING: No X11 application found for XWayland tests\n")
    io.stderr:write("  Tried: xterm, xeyes, xclock\n")
    io.stderr:write("  Install one of these to run XWayland tests\n")
    return false
end

--- Spawn an X11 test client with the given class.
-- @tparam[opt="xwayland_test"] string class The WM_CLASS for the client
-- @tparam[opt] string title The window title (may not be honored by all apps)
-- @treturn number|nil The PID of the spawned process, or nil on failure
local function spawn_x11_client(_, class, title)
    class = class or "xwayland_test"

    if not detect_x11_app() then
        io.stderr:write("ERROR: Cannot spawn X11 test client - no X11 app available\n")
        return nil
    end

    local exe = x11_app_cmd[1]
    local class_flag = x11_app_cmd[2]
    local exec_flag = x11_app_cmd[3]

    -- Build command based on what app we're using
    local cmd
    if exe == "xterm" then
        -- xterm: -class CLASS -name INSTANCE -T TITLE -e CMD
        cmd = string.format(
            "xterm -class %s -name %s -T '%s' -e 'sleep infinity'",
            class, class:lower(), title or class
        )
    elseif exe == "xeyes" or exe == "xclock" then
        -- These simple apps don't support class override easily,
        -- but we can still spawn them for basic XWayland testing
        cmd = exe
        io.stderr:write(string.format(
            "WARNING: %s doesn't support custom WM_CLASS, using default\n", exe
        ))
    else
        -- Generic fallback
        if class_flag then
            cmd = string.format("%s %s %s", exe, class_flag, class)
        else
            cmd = exe
        end
    end

    io.stderr:write(string.format("[X11] Spawning: %s\n", cmd))

    -- Spawn the client
    local pid = awful.spawn(cmd)

    if pid and type(pid) == "number" and pid > 0 then
        table.insert(spawned_pids, pid)
        return pid
    else
        io.stderr:write("ERROR: Failed to spawn X11 test client: " .. tostring(pid) .. "\n")
        return nil
    end
end

--- Terminate all spawned X11 test clients.
-- This should be called at the end of tests to clean up.
function module.terminate()
    for _, pid in ipairs(spawned_pids) do
        os.execute("kill " .. pid .. " 2>/dev/null")
    end
    spawned_pids = {}
end

--- Get the list of spawned PIDs.
-- @treturn table List of PIDs for spawned X11 test clients
function module.get_spawned_pids()
    return gears.table.clone(spawned_pids)
end

--- Check if an X11 application is available for spawning.
-- @treturn boolean True if an X11 app was detected
function module.is_available()
    return detect_x11_app()
end

--- Get info about the detected X11 application.
-- @treturn table|nil Table with app info or nil
function module.get_app_info()
    if detect_x11_app() then
        return {
            executable = x11_app_cmd[1],
            class_flag = x11_app_cmd[2],
            exec_flag = x11_app_cmd[3],
            default_class = x11_app_cmd[4],
        }
    end
    return nil
end

--- Get the default WM_CLASS for spawned X11 clients.
-- This is useful when the app doesn't support custom class names.
-- @treturn string|nil The default class name
function module.get_default_class()
    if detect_x11_app() then
        -- For xterm with custom class, return what we'll set
        if x11_app_cmd[1] == "xterm" then
            return nil -- We set custom class
        end
        return x11_app_cmd[4]
    end
    return nil
end

--- Check if a client is an XWayland client.
-- @tparam client c The client to check
-- @treturn boolean True if client is XWayland
function module.is_xwayland(c)
    -- XWayland clients have a window ID (X11 window)
    -- Native Wayland clients don't
    return c and c.window and c.window > 0
end

--- Find X11 clients by class.
-- @tparam string class The WM_CLASS to search for
-- @treturn table List of matching X11 clients
function module.find_by_class(class)
    local results = {}
    for _, c in ipairs(client.get()) do
        if c.class == class and module.is_xwayland(c) then
            table.insert(results, c)
        end
    end
    return results
end

-- Make the module callable for spawning clients
-- Usage: x11_client("MyXApp", "Window Title")
return setmetatable(module, { __call = spawn_x11_client })

local timer = require("gears.timer")
local gtable = require("gears.table")

local runner = {
    quit_awesome_on_error = os.getenv('TEST_PAUSE_ON_ERRORS') ~= '1',
}

-- Async module for coroutine-based tests (loaded lazily)
local async = nil

local verbose = os.getenv('VERBOSE') == '1'

-- Persistent mode: don't quit compositor after test
-- Set by shell script or test harness
local persistent_mode = false

--- Enable persistent mode (don't quit after test completion).
-- Call this before running tests in persistent mode.
function runner.set_persistent(enabled)
    persistent_mode = enabled
end

--- Check if running in persistent mode.
-- @treturn boolean True if persistent mode is enabled
function runner.is_persistent()
    return persistent_mode
end

-- Was the runner started already?
local running = false

-- This is used if a test causes errors before starting the runner
timer.start_new(1, function()
    if not running then
        io.stderr:write("Error: run_steps() was never called.\n")
        if not runner.quit_awesome_on_error then
            io.stderr:write("Keeping awesome open...\n")
            return  -- keep awesome open on error.
        end
        awesome.quit()
    end
end)

runner.step_kill_clients = function(step)
    if step == 1 then
        for _,c in ipairs(client.get()) do
            c:kill()
        end
    end
    if #client.get() == 0 then
        return true
    end
end

--- Print a message if verbose mode is enabled.
-- @tparam string message The message to print.
function runner.verbose(message)
    if verbose then
        io.stderr:write(message .. "\n")
    end
end

--- When using run_direct(), this function indicates that the test is now done.
-- @tparam[opt=nil] string message An error message explaining the test failure, if it failed.
function runner.done(message)
    if message then
        io.stderr:write("Error: " .. message .. "\n")
        if not runner.quit_awesome_on_error then
            io.stderr:write("Keeping awesome open...\n")
            return
        end
    end

    local client_count = #client.get()
    if client_count > 0 then
        io.stderr:write(string.format(
            "NOTE: there were %d clients left after the test.\n", client_count))

        -- Remove any clients (unless in persistent mode where _state.reset handles this)
        if not persistent_mode then
            for _,c in ipairs(client.get()) do
                c:kill()
            end
        end
    end

    if not message then
        io.stderr:write("Test finished successfully.\n")
    end

    -- In persistent mode, don't quit - just reset the running flag
    if persistent_mode then
        running = false
        return
    end

    awesome.quit()
end

--- This function is called to indicate that a test does not use the run_steps()
-- facility, but instead runs something else directly.
function runner.run_direct()
    -- In persistent mode, reset running flag to allow multiple tests
    if persistent_mode and running then
        running = false
    end
    assert(not running, "API abuse: Test was started twice")
    running = true
end

--- Reset runner state for a new test (used in persistent mode).
-- This is called by state.reset() to prepare for the next test.
function runner.reset_state()
    running = false
    if async then
        async._set_coroutine(nil)
    end
end

--- Start some step-wise tests. The given steps are called in order until all
-- succeeded. Each step is a function that can return true/false to indicate
-- success/failure, but can also return nothing if it needs to be called again
-- later.
function runner.run_steps(steps, options)
    options = gtable.crush({
        kill_clients=true,
        wait_per_step=2,  -- how long to wait per step in seconds.
    }, options or {})
    -- Setup timer/timeout to limit waiting for signal and quitting awesome.
    local t = timer({timeout=0})
    local wait=options.wait_per_step / 0.1
    local step=1
    local step_count=0
    runner.run_direct()

    if options.kill_clients then
        -- Add a final step to kill all clients and wait for them to finish.
        -- Ref: https://github.com/awesomeWM/awesome/pull/1904#issuecomment-312793006
        steps[#steps + 1] = runner.step_kill_clients
    end

    t:connect_signal("timeout", function() timer.delayed_call(function()
        local step_func = steps[step]
        step_count = step_count + 1
        local step_as_string = step..'/'..#steps..' (@'..step_count..')'

        io.flush()  -- for "tail -f".
        runner.verbose(string.format('Running step %s..\n', step_as_string))

        -- Call the current step's function.
        local success, result = xpcall(function()
            return step_func(step_count)
        end, debug.traceback)

        if not success then
            runner.done('running function for step '
                        ..step_as_string..': '..tostring(result)..'!')
            t:stop()
        elseif result then
            -- true: test succeeded.
            if step < #steps then
                -- Next step.
                step = step+1
                step_count = 0
                wait = options.wait_per_step / 0.1
                t.timeout = 0
                t:again()
            else
                -- All steps finished, we are done.
                runner.done()
            end
        else
            -- Append filename/lnum of failed step function.
            local step_info = debug.getinfo(step_func)
            local step_loc = string.format("%s:%d", step_info["short_src"], step_info["linedefined"])
            step_as_string = step_as_string .. " ("..step_loc..")"

            if result == false then
                runner.done("Step "..step_as_string.." failed (returned false).")
            else
                -- No result yet, run this step again.
                wait = wait-1
                if wait > 0 then
                    t.timeout = 0.1
                    t:again()
                else
                    runner.done("timeout waiting for signal in step "
                                ..step_as_string..".")
                    t:stop()
                end
            end
        end
    end) end)
    t:start()
end

--- Run a test using async/coroutine style.
-- This provides a cleaner API than run_steps() for tests that need
-- to wait for events. The test function runs as a coroutine and can
-- use async.wait_for_* functions to yield until events occur.
--
-- @tparam function test_fn The test function to run
-- @tparam[opt] table options Options table
-- @tparam[opt=true] boolean options.kill_clients Kill all clients after test
-- @usage
--     runner.run_async(function()
--         test_client("myapp")
--         local c = async.wait_for_client("myapp", 5)
--         assert(c, "Client did not appear")
--         runner.done()
--     end)
function runner.run_async(test_fn, options)
    options = gtable.crush({
        kill_clients = true,
    }, options or {})

    runner.run_direct()

    -- Load async module if not already loaded
    if not async then
        async = require("_async")
    end

    -- Wrap test function to handle completion
    local wrapped = function()
        local success, err = xpcall(test_fn, debug.traceback)
        if not success then
            runner.done("Test error: " .. tostring(err))
        end
        -- Note: test_fn should call runner.done() on success
    end

    -- Create coroutine for the test
    local co = coroutine.create(wrapped)

    -- Register with async module so wait_for_* functions can resume it
    async._set_coroutine(co)

    -- Start the coroutine (uses delayed_call to ensure event loop is running)
    timer.delayed_call(function()
        local ok, err = coroutine.resume(co)
        if not ok then
            runner.done("Failed to start test: " .. tostring(err))
        end
    end)
end

return runner

function utils.assert_geometry(actual, expected, tolerance)
    tolerance = tolerance or 0

    local function check(name, a, e)
        if e ~= nil then
            local diff = math.abs(a - e)
            if diff > tolerance then
                error(string.format(
                    "Geometry mismatch: %s expected %d, got %d (diff %d, tolerance %d)",
                    name, e, a, diff, tolerance

            end
        end
    end

    check("x", actual.x, expected.x)
    check("y", actual.y, expected.y)
    check("width", actual.width, expected.width)
    check("height", actual.height, expected.height)
end
